_readme: Hand-edited. The indexer NEVER writes this file.
After editing run: npm run index-faces:recluster  (seconds — detection is cached)
Applied in order: ignoreFaces/ignorePhotos -> split -> merge -> people attributes.
Person ids are stable across re-runs. See face-index/review.json for every
detected person, their photo count and the borderline pairs worth deciding on.

_schema.people: { "p-0001": { name, featured, order, cover, hidden, note } }
_schema.merge: [["p-0001","p-0003"]] — first id is canonical, the rest are absorbed

_mergeNotes: p-0003 is Nadav wearing sunglasses. Sunglasses destroy the eye region the
descriptor relies on, so it clustered separately (d=0.478 to p-0001) even
though p-0001 already contains other sunglasses shots of him. Verified by eye.
NOT merged, deliberately: p-0004, p-0005, p-0006, p-0012, p-0014, p-0017 and
p-0029 are all red-haired women who each sit 0.48-0.56 from Sharon (p-0002)
but 0.51-0.59 from EACH OTHER. That pattern means they are close to a large
cluster's broad centroid, not that they are one person. Check them in
face-index/review.json and merge only the ones you recognise.
